newsitem.title: CHINA: China group forms spot commodity exchange.
newsitem.headline: China group forms spot commodity exchange.

text.p: A Chinese investment group set up a commodity exchange that began trading spot contracts in metals, construction materials and agricultural products on Wednesday.
The Hua Yuan Commodity Exchange began trading contracts on its main Beijing trading floor, which is linked by satellite to trading centres in Shanghai, Shenzhen and Haikou.
Members can trade contracts of aluminium, copper, green beans, coffee, wheat, plywood and rubber -- most of them in lots of one tonne.
Price movements are capped at 10 percent above or below the previous day's average level.
The sponsor of the exchange is the Hua Yuan Investment Group, which includes futures trader, Hua Yuan Futures Ltd.
Gao Yang, a Hua Yuan planning department executive, told Reuters at the opening ceremonies that the exchange had about 100 members.
Futures trading has come under tightened scrutiny from China's regulatory authorities and many of the existing exchanges have found a steep decline in business.
Many commodities brokers posted losses last year, according to industry officials.
Exchange officials were optimistic that spot commodities trading would not face such problems.
